intro: Convert meters (or metres) to feet accurately for building heights, athletic tracks, elevation maps, and civil engineering plans. Because 1 international foot equals exactly 0.3048 meters, multiplying meters by 3.2808399 (or dividing by 0.3048) returns exact feet. For geodetic land surveys requiring meters to survey feet, multiply by 3.2808333 (1200/3937 m). Check pre-computed spans in the meter to feet conversion chart below.
alsoWrittenAs: m to ft, metres to feet, meter to foot, m into ft, meters to US survey feet

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: International Feet vs. US Survey Feet (meters to survey ft)
items: Standard engineering, aviation, and height conversions use the International Foot (0.3048 m exact, so 1 m = 3.280839895 ft). Legacy US geodetic surveying uses the US Survey Foot (1200/3937 m ≈ 0.30480061 m, so 1 m = 3.280833333 US survey ft).
The two definitions differ by only 2 parts per million (~0.0066 ft at 1,000 m, or ~0.01 ft per mile), which matters only in large state-plane coordinate systems.

faqs.question: How many feet are in 1 meter?
faqs.answer: 1 meter equals 3.28084 international feet (1 ÷ 0.3048 = 3.2808399 ft), or roughly 3 feet 3.37 inches.

faqs.question: What is the difference between meters to international feet and meters to US survey feet?
faqs.answer: International feet use 1 ft = 0.3048 m exact (1 m = 3.2808399 ft), whereas US survey feet use 1200/3937 m (1 m = 3.2808333 US survey ft)—a 2 ppm difference of roughly 0.0066 ft per 1,000 meters.

faqs.question: How do I convert meters to feet?
faqs.answer: Divide meters by 0.3048, or multiply by 3.28084. For example, 85 m × 3.2808399 = 278.87139 ft.

faqs.question: What is 8,849 meters (Mount Everest) in feet?
faqs.answer: 8,849 meters equals 29,032.15223 feet (often rounded to 29,032 ft).
